evidence_frontier.observation: In the most recent confirmation (PNN‑v1‑W8‑Confirmation) the w8 candidate achieved 424 correct predictions on the ECG200 test set (100 samples × 5 seeds) while the w16 control achieved 441 correct. The w8 candidate fell 17 correct predictions short of the control, violating the preregistered relative gate (candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10).
evidence_frontier.hypothesis: Training the w8 configuration for more epochs (100 instead of 50) will improve its aggregate Q.ANT correct count sufficiently to meet the relative gate (candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10) without altering any other architectural elements.

analysis: Observation: The w8 boundary was not confirmed under the original training regime (50 epochs), showing a consistent accuracy gap of ~3 % relative to w16. Hypothesis: Extending training duration may allow the narrower local representation to converge better, reducing the gap. This hypothesis is falsifiable: if after 100 epochs the w8 candidate still falls more than 10 correct predictions behind the w16 control, the hypothesis is rejected.
hypothesis: Increasing training epochs to 100 will enable the Alpha5 w8 configuration to achieve an aggregate Q.ANT correct count within 10 of the Alpha5 w16 control on ECG200 under a fresh seed set.

proposal.title: Extended‑Epoch Confirmation of the w8 Local‑Width Boundary on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does training the Alpha5 w8 configuration for 100 epochs close the performance gap to the Alpha5 w16 control on ECG200?
proposal.rationale: The prior w8 confirmation failed under a 50‑epoch regime, leaving open whether the gap is due to insufficient training rather than an inherent capacity limit. Demonstrating that longer training can meet the relative gate would inform future width‑compression decisions and model‑size trade‑offs.

procedure: Define a fresh set of five independent random seeds [42,43,44,45,46].
For each seed, train the Alpha5 w8 candidate for 100 epochs on the ECG200 training split (100 samples).
For the same seed, train the Alpha5 w16 control for 100 epochs under identical hyper‑parameters.
After training, evaluate both models on the ECG200 test split (100 samples) and record the number of correct Q.ANT predictions per seed.
Aggregate correct counts across the five seeds for candidate and control (max 500).
Apply the relative success criterion: candidate_correct ≥ control_correct − 10.

success_criteria.relative_gate: candidate_correct >= control_correct - 10 on the aggregated 5*100 predictions

proposal.risks: Longer training may increase over‑fitting on the small ECG200 training set; additional compute time may delay downstream experiments; results remain limited to software‑simulation and cannot be extrapolated to physical photonic hardware.
